Q682296.summary: This bishop's throne is entirely sheathed in carved ivory. On the front, John the Baptist, holding a medallion of the Lamb of God, stands between the four evangelists beneath Maximian's monogram, framed by vines inhabited by animals; on the high rounded back, panels tell the story of Christ's infancy and life, and on the sides the story of Joseph. Christ is thus present both as the Lamb proclaimed by the Baptist and in the Gospel scenes behind the bishop's head.
facts: It was made for Archbishop Maximian of Ravenna, who is named by his monogram on the front, and is the largest single surviving Late Antique work in ivory.
Of the 24 panels on the back, only 16 survive or have been restored.
Scholars still debate whether it was carved in Constantinople or Alexandria; differences in style suggest several carvers.
Q682296.notes: The individual back panels are small in the thumbnail; Christ's appearances there were not individually confirmed from the image. Dating c. 545–553 per Wikipedia.
